findings.description: The bucket is explicitly documented as public with no ACL restricting access, allowing unauthenticated or unintended access to stored objects including the customer-master.xlsx data file.
No server-side encryption configuration (SSE-S3/SSE-KMS) is applied to the bucket, leaving stored objects unencrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled, so accidental or malicious deletion/overwrite of objects (including sensitive customer data) cannot be recovered from, increasing impact of an attack or misconfiguration.
A sensitive customer master data file is stored in the aws_s3_bucket.data bucket which is public and unencrypted, directly exposing customer PII/financial data to unauthorized access.
No server-side encryption configuration is applied to this bucket holding financial data, leaving sensitive financial records unencrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled on a bucket storing financial data, so malicious or accidental deletion/overwrite cannot be recovered from.

The bucket does not define a server_side_encryption_configuration block, meaning objects stored are not encrypted at rest by default, risking exposure of sensitive data if the bucket or underlying storage is compromised.
The bucket has no logging block configured, so there is no audit trail of access requests, hampering detection of unauthorized access attempts (defense-in-depth gap).
The bucket does not define a server_side_encryption_configuration block, so stored objects are not encrypted at rest, exposing potentially sensitive data-science datasets if storage is compromised.
